chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Salat over جنازة is disliked when the sun turns yellow and when it rises.
So this report is explicit in indicating dislike rather than prohibition, and it is possible that its basis is taqiyyah, because that is the position of the generality.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةَ: dissimulation or precaution in expression due to prevailing circumstances
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the funeral salat being discussed in this report
key_terms.الْجَنَائِزِ: the deceased persons over whom the funeral salat is performed
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni majority view in this context
key_terms.تُكْرَهُ: indicates that the act is disliked, not strictly forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is salat over the deceased prohibited or merely disliked at sunrise and when the sun turns yellow?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on performing salat over the deceased at the time of sunrise and when the sun yellows. It indicates karahah rather than prohibition, and notes the possibility that the report reflects taqiyyah due to its agreement with the view of the generality.
